title: Nectar robbing from Hibiscus flowers by White-eyes on an oceanic island, Chichi-jima, Bonin Islands
orientation_basis: larger flower size -> higher robbery frequency
evidence_basis: Primary report states that larger Hibiscus flowers were robbed more often than smaller flowers.
notes: Reward covaries with flower size, so this is a direct geometry-pattern code rather than evidence that access cost alone caused the relation.

title: Geographic Variation in Flower Size and Flower-Visitor Composition of Two Bumblebee-Pollinated, Spring-Flowering Herbs, Lamium album L. var. barbatum (Lamiaceae) and Meehania urticifolia (Lamiaceae)
orientation_basis: larger/more protective calyx geometry -> lower robbery; severe robbery occurs in the smaller-calxy population
evidence_basis: Primary study reports severe robbery in the population with shorter/narrower calyxes and a significant within-population association of calyx width and CL×CW with bite-mark presence; discussion identifies the calyx as a physical barrier to robber entry.
notes: This is a bypass-protection boundary case, not evidence that larger calyx dimensions increase legitimate-route difficulty.
